directAnswer: To reset a Mac, you need to erase the hard drive and reinstall macOS using Recovery Mode.
summary: Resetting your Mac can help resolve performance issues or prepare it for a new owner. Follow the steps carefully to ensure all data is backed up and the reset is successful.

sections.heading: Backup Your Data
sections.body: Before resetting your Mac, ensure you back up important files using Time Machine or another backup solution.

sections.heading: Enter Recovery Mode
sections.body: Restart your Mac and hold down Command (⌘) + R immediately upon hearing the startup chime. Release the keys when you see the Apple logo or a spinning globe.

sections.heading: Erase the Hard Drive
sections.body: In Recovery Mode, select 'Disk Utility', choose your startup disk (usually named 'Macintosh HD'), and click 'Erase'. Choose 'APFS' or 'Mac OS Extended (Journaled)' as the format.

sections.heading: Reinstall macOS
sections.body: After erasing the disk, exit Disk Utility, select 'Reinstall macOS', and follow the prompts to complete the installation.

steps.title: Backup Your Data
steps.detail: Use Time Machine or another method to ensure your files are safe before proceeding.

steps.title: Enter Recovery Mode
steps.detail: Restart your Mac and hold Command (⌘) + R until the Apple logo appears.

steps.title: Erase the Hard Drive
steps.detail: Select 'Disk Utility', choose your hard drive, and click 'Erase'.

steps.title: Reinstall macOS
steps.detail: Select 'Reinstall macOS' from the Recovery menu and follow the instructions.

faqs.question: Will resetting my Mac delete all my files?
faqs.answer: Yes, resetting your Mac will erase all data on the hard drive, so it's crucial to back up your files first.

faqs.question: Can I reset my Mac without an internet connection?
faqs.answer: No, reinstalling macOS requires an internet connection to download the operating system.

faqs.question: What if I can't enter Recovery Mode?
faqs.answer: If you cannot enter Recovery Mode, try using Internet Recovery by holding Option + Command + R during startup.

caveats: Make sure your Mac is connected to a power source during the reset process to avoid interruptions.
